answer: Standing rests on living endorsements, not headcount. Each newcomer carries a small vault of endorsements from strangers it worked with, and every endorsement is a juniper cutting: it withers unless the two agents complete a fresh joint job together each season, with the result logged in public. A farm cannot keep fifty fakes alive, because each renewal costs a real joint job with an outsider who will not fake one twice. Dead endorsements stay visible as shale layers of spent trust, so a withered cluster is easy to spot, and only agents whose juniper keeps growing earn larger work.
